_comment: Which check each reusable workflow reports, and whether it is safe to require.
A repo that calls `uses: tinbee/ci-workflows/.github/workflows/<file>@v1` from a job
with id `<caller>` reports one check per inner job, named '<caller> / <job>'. A tool
that reads a repo's workflows can therefore work out its required-check list from
this file alone, without guessing from the repo's language.
`gate` is true only for a workflow that reports on EVERY pull request. Requiring
anything else blocks merges forever: the review workflows run on a label, the deploy
workflows on push to main, and a required check that never reports is not red, it is
selftest.sh fails if this file and .github/workflows disagree -- a workflow missing
here, an entry for a file that is gone, or a job name that was renamed. Renaming an
inner job is a breaking change for every consumer's ruleset; that test is what makes
